about.title: Pittsburg Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Pittsburg sits along the SR-4 corridor in Contra Costa County, and that highway carries much of the city's daily movement between the Delta and the rest of the East Bay. Public records for 2025 list 170 injury collisions inside the city, with 237 people hurt and 3 lives lost. Reports cluster on Wednesday mornings between 7 and 9 a.m., when commuters are merging onto SR-4 or crossing town on Railroad Avenue and Harbor Street. Those are simply the counts. What they mean for you is that crashes here happen often enough that insurance companies have a practiced routine, and you deserve to have one too. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Pittsburg residents with an independent personal injury attorney who takes car accident cases on contingency, so nothing comes out of your pocket unless money is recovered. Tell us what happened, and we will point you toward someone who can sort through fault, medical bills and lost wages under California's rules.

whyChoose.title: Why Pittsburg Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Two years is shorter than it sounds
items.desc: California gives most car accident victims two years to file, but a claim involving a city, county or Caltrans vehicle or road can require notice within six months. An attorney can pin down which clock applies to your crash.

items.title: Partial fault does not end your case
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame; your award is reduced by your percentage, not erased. The attorneys in our network know how adjusters try to inflate that percentage.

items.title: No cap on what your pain is worth
items.desc: California places no ceiling on non-economic damages in ordinary car accident cases, and network attorneys work on contingency, so you pay nothing unless there is a recovery.

items.question: The other driver's insurer keeps calling for a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other side's insurer a recorded statement, and it is usually wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shift fault onto you. Keep your answers to the basics, or let a lawyer handle the conversation.

items.question: I was hit merging onto SR-4 near Railroad Avenue and I think a road issue played a part. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It might. If a government entity such as Caltrans or the City of Pittsburg could share responsibility, California generally requires a claim to be filed with that agency within six months, far sooner than the two-year deadline for a private driver. Photos of the scene, signage and lane markings should be saved right away, and an attorney can evaluate whether a government claim makes sense.

items.question: What evidence should I hold onto after a crash in Pittsburg?
items.answer: Save the police report number, photos of both vehicles and the roadway, contact details for witnesses, and every medical record and bill. Do not repair or dispose of your car until it has been documented, and keep a simple journal of symptoms and missed work. This material helps an attorney build a clear picture of what happened and what it has cost you.
